title: Network Analysis of Working Memory in Young Adults Following a Single Session of Transcranial Pulse Stimulation
summary:
Ultrasound therapies have been used in medicine for many years—for example, to promote wound healing or for pain management.
Building on this, a new procedure for the brain has been developed: transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS). In this procedure, very short, weak acoustic shock waves (related to ultrasound waves) are transmitted through the skull. This allows the functions of specific brain regions to be stimulated without surgery . This study aims to investigate how a single TPS stimulation session affects the working memory of young, healthy individuals.

interventions.name: The study examines the modulation of the working memory network in healthy participants who receive a single session of transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) (30 minutes with 4,000 pulses). Procedure per session: 1. Baseline fMRI scan 2. TPS stimulation 3. Follow-up fMRI scan. (Total measurement dura

In comparison, the same healthy participants receive a single session of placebo transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) (30 minutes with 4,000 pulses, but using a sham cap). The washout period between the two sessions is 2 weeks, and the type of stimulation assigned to the two sessions is randomized.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Good knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
-Pre-existing neurological or psychiatric conditions
-Use of centrally acting medications
-Epilepsy
-Pregnant or breastfeeding women
-Individuals with implants that are not compatible with MRI or TPS
-Contraindications for TPS use (thrombosis, blood clotting disorders, corticosteroid treatment within 6 weeks prior to TPS stimulation)
